programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing 's Coco a' feuchainn air diofar dhòighean eagal a chur air daoine 's iad a toirt air Flop leum! Ged 's e spòrs uabhasach a th' ann dhaibhsan, chan eil Charlie a cheart cho measail air a gheama seo! Bing and Coco are trying different ways of scaring people and take great delight in making Flop jump! However, poor Charlie doesn't see the funny side as much as the others!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha dèideag ùr air nochdadh san sgoil-altraim aig Amma, dèideag mhìorbhailteach a bhios a bruidhinn! Ge-tà, chan eil an dèideag seo a cheart cho tarraingeach nuair a dh'fhàsas iad uile sgìth de bhith 'g èisteachd ris an aon duan…! A new toy has appeared at Amma's creche, an exciting new toy car that talks! However, the toy becomes less and less appealing as everyone gets impatient with listening to the same thing over and over again!

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: 'S toigh le na h-Abadas a bhith cluich falach-fead. Tha am facal ùr cuideachd comasach air rudan a lorg nuair nach urrainn am faicinn. Dè th'ann agus cò an Abadas a b'fheàrr airson am facal a lorg? The Abadas love playing hide-and-seek. The day's word is also able to seek out things that can't be seen. What could it be and which Abada would be the best one to go and look for the word?

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha Àtaidh a’ dèanamh aran brochain, ach tha e a’ fàilleachdainn air an reasabaidh fhaighinn ceart. Dè nì e leis na tha e air a dhèanamh de dh’aran? Abney is making Porridge bread, but he just can't get the recipe right. What will he do with all these spare loaves?

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Bidh Latha na Cloinne ann a dh’aithghearr agus tha Peicein is a charaidean a’ cur romhpa tuairmsean a thoirt dham pàrantan a thaobh na preusantan a tha iad ag iarraidh. Ged nach eil iad a’ faighinn na bha iad ag iarraidh, tha iad ag iomlaid nam preusantan aca le chèile, is aig deireadh an latha tha iad a’ faighinn na bha iad ag iarraidh. Children’s Day is approaching, and Petit and his friends decide they will give their parents clues on what gifts they want. Even though the youngsters don't receive their exact wishes, they end up exchanging presents to get what they all wanted.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ leughadh Far a bheil na Rudan Fiadhaich. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Maurice Sendak agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Mòrag Stiùbhart. A bedtime story for young children. Ramsay MacMahon reads Far a bheil na Rudan Fiadhaich, written by Maurice Sendak and translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: The Deep/An Doimhne
programme.desc: Tha seann teampall falaichte le ìomhaighean annasach na dhìomhaireas do Na Neachdan an-diugh. Às bi dè eile, an aire air na freiceadanan! A strange hidden ancient temple with unusual statues is a mystery to the Neachdan today. Whatever else, beware the sentinels!

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha an Treud a' cluinntinn bhana nan reòiteagan air fàire agus a' tighinn an àrd le plana faighinn thuice. Leis an dràibhear a' faighinn cuideachadh, tha na caoraich air an dòigh le reòiteagan gun chrìoch - ach saoil am faigh daoine a-mach dè rinn iad? The flock hear the enticing tunes of an ice cream van approaching and quickly hatch a plan to divert it into their field. While the driver seeks help, the flock have great fun with an endless supply of ice cream. But will they be able to cover their tracks before they're discovered?

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha an t-uisge dheth ann am flat nam Ploc. Tha seachdainean bhon a thug Pòl boiseag nighidh dha fhèin mu dheireadh, is tha e air a chuir sìos dhan ìoslach a dh’fhaicinn gu dè a tha ceàrr air na pìoban uisge. Shìos an sin tha e a’ coinneachadh ri Seoc Sùbailte, fear eile nach bi ga nighe fhèin, is tha esan ga fhiathachadh dhan bhuidheann spèilidh aige, Na Clàbaraich. Tha dà riaghailt aig Na Clàbaraich: bidh iad a’ spèileadh agus tha samh asta. The water in the Spuds’ flat is off, and having not had a bath in weeks, Dave is sent down to the basement to find the problem. There Dave stumbles across a fellow stinker, Josh Gnarly, who invites him to join his skating gang, the NeverCleans. The group have one motto, they skate and they stink.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha am peata òr-iasg aig Pòl a’ tighinn beò a-rithist is ri miastadh. Dave’s pet goldfish returns from the dead to wreak havoc.

programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra
programme.desc: Mairi Rodgers explores Falkland Palace Garden in Fife. Tha Màiri Rodgers a’ gabhail cuairt tro Ghàrradh Lùchairt Falkland.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: How Seona McClintock became fluent in the language, and Calum Maclean heads out to sea with a hard-working crew who have saved many lives.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Fuine
programme.desc: Inspired by trips to fancy Italian cafes, Gregor shows us how he puts his own twist on cannoli.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses
programme.desc: Tha Còmhraidhean Ceimigeach a’ toirt sùil air mar a tha beathaichean a’ dèananmh feum de bhlas agus fàileadh airson conaltradh agus maireachdainn beò ann an dòighean do-chreidsinneach. This epiosde tunes into how animals use taste and smell to survive and communicate in ways that defy belief. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Seata cuirme le Rory Matheson Dance Band le Graham’s Jigs agus Irish Reels. Clàraichte beò aig Duaisean nan Trads 2025 ann an Obar Dheathain. Concert set performed by Rory Matheson Dance Band, featuring the tracks Graham’s Jigs and Irish Reels. Originally recorded live at the 2025 Trad Awards in Aberdeen.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: ’S urrainn do dhòigh-beatha Ayurvedic, a tha 3000 bliadhna a dh’aois, a bhith buannachdail dha do shlàinte. Tha na seòid a’ sireadh comhairle bho neach-iùil iòga agus a’ tilleadh dhan chidsin gus reasabaidhean cothromach a dhèanamh. A’ cumail slàinte Ruairidh nan inntinn, tha iad ag ullachadh Kitchari, Coiridh Goan le Muasgain-caola, Coiridh Glasraich air a dhèanamh ann an aon soitheach, Naan gun Ghràin, Mousse Teòclaid Aquafaba agus gus crìoch a chuir air seo uile, Teatha Chai. The 3,000-year-old Ayurvedic approach to life can be beneficial to health. The lads seek some advice from a yoga instructor and return to the kitchen to prepare some balanced recipes. Keeping Roddy’s best interests in mind, they prepare kitchari, Goan prawn curry, a one-pot vegetarian curry, grain-free naan, an aquafaba chocolate mousse and to finish, chai tea. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Tiugainn a Dhannsa
programme.desc: Thànaig crìoch air earrann de dh'eachdraidh chur-seachadan na Gàidhealtachd is nan Eilean nuair a dhùin tallachan -baile ann an iomadh ceàrnaidh. Chaidh tallachan ur an àrda ach is ann ag amas air feumalachdan ginealach ur a bha iad sin. Tha am prògram seo a' toirt beò a' rithist talla-bhaile. Dìreach mar thogalach sam bith eile tron là ach nuair a thuiteadh an oidhche agus a' thigeadh na brògan dannsa a-mach a bha mar saoghal eile. Documenting the place of village halls at the heart of communities across Scotland throughout the 20th century. The tearing down of old village halls across the Highlands and Islands marks the end of an era. Balivanich, Carinish, Acharacle, Lochmaddy, Leverburgh, Shawbost, Vatersay, Aird, Ness, the Highlanders' Institute - many halls have been replaced by buildings which focus their attention on the needs of a very different generation. The programme is illustrated with hilarious and often nostalgic anecdotes of these special places, so small and unimpressive by the light of day, but which were transformed by night into meccas of music and dance.

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: Suidhichte taobh a-staigh Cearcall na h-Artaig, tha Eileanan Lofoten ann an Nirribhidh a’ tabhann luach fad-beatha de thoileachas don luchd-turais a bhitheas a’ tadhal ann. Air a tharraing leis an t-sreap agus an surfadh air leth a tha ri fhaotainn ann, tha Coinneach MacFhraing a’ siubhal timcheall nan eilean còmhla ri a chompanach, Calum Gibb, gus eòlas fhaighinn air an t-àite miorbhaileach seo. Situated within the Arctic Circle, Norway’s Lofoten islands offer a lifetime’s worth of exploration in the outdoors. Attracted by the world-class climbing and surfing on offer, Coinneach Rankin journeys around the islands with his companion, Calum Gibb, to glean unique experiences.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Final of the quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take players so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. It is all about making connections between things which may appear, at first glance, not to be connected at all.

programme.title: Murder on the Victorian Railway
programme.desc: London 1864. On a Hackney bound train, a guard discovers blood in a first-class carriage - and a body on the railway embankment. For the first time, a murder has taken place on Britain's railways. Over a hundred years later, this single documentary for BBC Two uses the first-hand testimony of the people involved at the time to explore this unique event and how it provoked a huge public outcry and debate. The story quickly became a news sensation as the dangers of the brave new world of the train were laid bare. Over a hundred years later, the witnesses to this story may be long dead but their words survive in court transcripts, memoirs, letters and vivid journalism. These testimonies are now used to tell the story, taking the documentary deep into the 19th century to meet an extraordinary cross section of real-life Victorian London - from the engine driver who found the body to the detective in charge of the investigation. Who killed Mr Briggs?

programme.desc: Two more of round one’s highest-scoring losing teams have a second chance to qualify for the second round. Jeremy Paxman asks the questions.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take players so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. A team of three lads from the Cambridge Quiz Society pit their wits against a trio of Oxford Librarians with specialisms as diverse as Comparative Slavonic Linguistics, Classics and Theology. They compete to draw together the connections between things which, at first glance, seem utterly random, from Goldeneye to The Kilns to Hill Top to Haworth Parsonage.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: Marilyn Monroe was, and perhaps will always be, Hollywood’s biggest female film icon and the sexiest of cinema's sex symbols, lighting up the screen in several cinema classics – including one of cinema’s greatest comedies, Some Like It Hot. The aura surrounding her has been enhanced by a sense of mystery that comes from the fact she was very rarely interviewed. But anyone who knew or worked with her was guaranteed to be asked about their personal 'Marilyn moments'. Here we tell Marilyn's story through the insights and anecdotes of friends, directors and fellow actors who spoke about her over the years on a selection of BBC programmes. With archive interviews featuring stars like Jane Russell, Jack Lemmon and Tony Curtis, as well as directors like Billy Wilder and John Huston, and Marilyn's former husband Arthur Miller, these conversations paint a picture of a star who conquered Hollywood despite serious battles with her inner demons, and reveal what it was like for those who got to enter into the orbit of one of cinema's greatest stars.

programme.title: Some Like It Hot
programme.desc: 1929. Musicians Joe and Jerry accidentally witness the St Valentine's Day massacre. The boys decide to make a getaway by joining a jazz band heading for Florida. There's just one problem - it's an all-girl group. A comic masterpiece from director Wilder, with memorable performances.

programme.title: Nobody's Perfect: The Making of Some Like It Hot
programme.desc: Revealing documentary about the creation and shooting of the acclaimed comedy movie Some Like It Hot. Stars Jack Lemmon and Tony Curtis - and other members of the cast and crew, including producer Walter Mirisch - remember the making of writer-director Billy Wilder's classic film. Using extraordinary behind-the-scenes colour footage and candid on-set photographs taken by stills photographer Richard Miller (also interviewed), the documentary provides a surprisingly intimate and revealing but nevertheless hilarious portrait of the making of one of Hollywood's best-loved and greatest films.

programme.title: My Week with Marilyn
programme.desc: It is 1956, and The Prince and the Showgirl is being made at Pinewood Studios in London, directed by and starring Laurence Olivier, who has recruited one of the biggest Hollywood stars of all time, Marilyn Monroe, to co-star with him. Colin Clark, a junior assistant on the production, is assigned the job of looking after Marilyn and keeps a journal about the week he spent with her. It proves to be a turbulent experience as Marilyn is going through marital problems with her husband and uses Colin as a much-needed sounding board for all her pent-up neurosis. Acclaimed drama from BBC Films based on Clark's real-life diaries.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Final of the quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take players so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. It is all about making connections between things which may appear, at first glance, not to be connected at all.

programme.title: Murder on the Victorian Railway
programme.desc: London 1864. On a Hackney bound train, a guard discovers blood in a first-class carriage - and a body on the railway embankment. For the first time, a murder has taken place on Britain's railways. Over a hundred years later, this single documentary for BBC Two uses the first-hand testimony of the people involved at the time to explore this unique event and how it provoked a huge public outcry and debate. The story quickly became a news sensation as the dangers of the brave new world of the train were laid bare. Over a hundred years later, the witnesses to this story may be long dead but their words survive in court transcripts, memoirs, letters and vivid journalism. These testimonies are now used to tell the story, taking the documentary deep into the 19th century to meet an extraordinary cross section of real-life Victorian London - from the engine driver who found the body to the detective in charge of the investigation. Who killed Mr Briggs?

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take players so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. A team of three lads from the Cambridge Quiz Society pit their wits against a trio of Oxford Librarians with specialisms as diverse as Comparative Slavonic Linguistics, Classics and Theology. They compete to draw together the connections between things which, at first glance, seem utterly random, from Goldeneye to The Kilns to Hill Top to Haworth Parsonage.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: Marilyn Monroe was, and perhaps will always be, Hollywood’s biggest female film icon and the sexiest of cinema's sex symbols, lighting up the screen in several cinema classics – including one of cinema’s greatest comedies, Some Like It Hot. The aura surrounding her has been enhanced by a sense of mystery that comes from the fact she was very rarely interviewed. But anyone who knew or worked with her was guaranteed to be asked about their personal 'Marilyn moments'. Here we tell Marilyn's story through the insights and anecdotes of friends, directors and fellow actors who spoke about her over the years on a selection of BBC programmes. With archive interviews featuring stars like Jane Russell, Jack Lemmon and Tony Curtis, as well as directors like Billy Wilder and John Huston, and Marilyn's former husband Arthur Miller, these conversations paint a picture of a star who conquered Hollywood despite serious battles with her inner demons, and reveal what it was like for those who got to enter into the orbit of one of cinema's greatest stars.

programme.title: Some Like It Hot
programme.desc: 1929. Musicians Joe and Jerry accidentally witness the St Valentine's Day massacre. The boys decide to make a getaway by joining a jazz band heading for Florida. There's just one problem - it's an all-girl group. A comic masterpiece from director Wilder, with memorable performances.

programme.title: Nobody's Perfect: The Making of Some Like It Hot
programme.desc: Revealing documentary about the creation and shooting of the acclaimed comedy movie Some Like It Hot. Stars Jack Lemmon and Tony Curtis - and other members of the cast and crew, including producer Walter Mirisch - remember the making of writer-director Billy Wilder's classic film. Using extraordinary behind-the-scenes colour footage and candid on-set photographs taken by stills photographer Richard Miller (also interviewed), the documentary provides a surprisingly intimate and revealing but nevertheless hilarious portrait of the making of one of Hollywood's best-loved and greatest films.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: AI Decoded examines a dramatic week for Elon Musk that could reshape the future of artificial intelligence. A US court has rejected Musk's claims against OpenAI, bringing a long-running feud with co-founder Sam Altman into sharp focus and offering a rare glimpse inside one of the world's most influential AI companies. At the same time, SpaceX is preparing for what could be the largest stock market listing in history - a move that may value the company at up to $1.75 trillion and make Musk the world's first human trillionaire.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee and Diarmuid are in Croydon to help sisters Lynette and Natalie rescue their vast, sun-baked plot, where weeds have taken over, veggie beds are impossible to reach and a polytunnel and pallets leave little room for peace. The sisters dream of a retreat garden where they can reconnect with nature – a hidden, tranquil space filled with scents, sounds and colour. They’d love raised, no-dig beds for veggies and propagation, plus a spot to sit and just relax. Having spent the last 18 months living together and supporting their community through wilderness gardening projects, Lynette and Natalie are ready to create a sanctuary of their own. Can the team transform this cluttered space into a peaceful retreat for £5,500?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Louise, Emily, Laura and Beth – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Escape to the Country

The exciting property line-up includes a mystery house that has six centuries of stories to tell, some of which are written on its walls! Aside from ancient houses, Briony is excited to meet a fellow baking enthusiast who, after making his own escape to the county a year ago, now sells cakes and runs a supper club from his home.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee and Diarmuid are in Croydon to help sisters Lynette and Natalie rescue their vast, sun-baked plot, where weeds have taken over, veggie beds are impossible to reach and a polytunnel and pallets leave little room for peace. The sisters dream of a retreat garden where they can reconnect with nature – a hidden, tranquil space filled with scents, sounds and colour. They’d love raised, no-dig beds for veggies and propagation, plus a spot to sit and just relax. Having spent the last 18 months living together and supporting their community through wilderness gardening projects, Lynette and Natalie are ready to create a sanctuary of their own. Can the team transform this cluttered space into a peaceful retreat for £5,500?

Aside from ancient houses, Briony is excited to meet a fellow baking enthusiast who, after making his own escape to the county a year ago, now sells cakes and runs a supper club from his home.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee and Diarmuid are in Croydon to help sisters Lynette and Natalie rescue their vast, sun-baked plot, where weeds have taken over, veggie beds are impossible to reach and a polytunnel and pallets leave little room for peace. The sisters dream of a retreat garden where they can reconnect with nature – a hidden, tranquil space filled with scents, sounds and colour. They’d love raised, no-dig beds for veggies and propagation, plus a spot to sit and just relax. Having spent the last 18 months living together and supporting their community through wilderness gardening projects, Lynette and Natalie are ready to create a sanctuary of their own. Can the team transform this cluttered space into a peaceful retreat for £5,500?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Louise, Emily, Laura and Beth – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Ria Lina. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee and Diarmuid are in Croydon to help sisters Lynette and Natalie rescue their vast, sun-baked plot, where weeds have taken over, veggie beds are impossible to reach and a polytunnel and pallets leave little room for peace. The sisters dream of a retreat garden where they can reconnect with nature – a hidden, tranquil space filled with scents, sounds and colour. They’d love raised, no-dig beds for veggies and propagation, plus a spot to sit and just relax. Having spent the last 18 months living together and supporting their community through wilderness gardening projects, Lynette and Natalie are ready to create a sanctuary of their own. Can the team transform this cluttered space into a peaceful retreat for £5,500?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Louise, Emily, Laura and Beth – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee and Diarmuid are in Croydon to help sisters Lynette and Natalie rescue their vast, sun-baked plot, where weeds have taken over, veggie beds are impossible to reach and a polytunnel and pallets leave little room for peace. The sisters dream of a retreat garden where they can reconnect with nature – a hidden, tranquil space filled with scents, sounds and colour. They’d love raised, no-dig beds for veggies and propagation, plus a spot to sit and just relax. Having spent the last 18 months living together and supporting their community through wilderness gardening projects, Lynette and Natalie are ready to create a sanctuary of their own. Can the team transform this cluttered space into a peaceful retreat for £5,500?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Louise, Emily, Laura and Beth – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents this high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring rugby player and podcaster Joe Marler, actor Jennie McAlpine, comedian Geoff Norcott and presenter Jean Johannson as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Wild Cameramen at Work
programme.desc: In the last of this spectacular series on the work of the world's top wildlife film-makers we enter the literally breathtaking environment of the ocean depths. Cameramen Doug Anderson and Doug Allan reveal the technical challenges of filming beneath the waves and encounter animals as diverse as blue whales, white-tip sharks and the unforgettably named weedy sea dragon - a tiny creature whose courtship dance is as tender and graceful as any ballet.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Some more unusual methods of growing are demonstrated at Beechgrove Garden. Ruth Vichos attempts to produce a mushroom crop and there’s a report on some of Scotland’s best bonsai, with everything you need to know to start that form or cultivation. Brian Cunningham is in the Seaside Garden at Beechgrove refreshing the planting with varieties that can withstand a coastal climate and Brian turns conifers into sculptures with topiary. Plus the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Landward

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: On a Bradford estate, Lenny and Mullet find an abandoned car and turn it into a DIY spaceship. A kitchen-sink science fiction comedy about estate childhoods, big dreams and escaping without going anywhere.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: After solving the Andie Bell case, Pip is forced to confront the consequences of what her investigation exposed. It may have cleared Sal’s name, but it tore Cara’s family apart, and the guilt weighs heavily on Pip. In an attempt to rebuild her relationship with Cara, Pip releases a podcast to tell the world the real story. The only person yet to face justice is Max Hastings, and as his trial approaches, Pip is determined to help his victims find closure. However, the prosecution’s case begins to falter when Becca Bell withdraws from testifying. Unwilling to accept this, Pip musters the courage to visit Becca in prison with the hope of convincing her that giving evidence still matters. Pip wants to focus on supporting Ravi at the upcoming memorial for his brother, but when a mysterious note promising information on Max appears in her locker, Pip must make a difficult decision. Little Kilton comes together to say goodbye to both Andie Bell and Sal Singh. The end of one dark chapter gives way to another, as Cara finds herself in a dangerous situation, and Jamie Reynolds, Connor’s brother and a key witness in Max’s trial, disappears without warning.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip hits a dead end and rethinks. Digging into Jamie’s recent behaviour and last movements, she realises he may not be an innocent victim after all.

programme.title: The Catch Up
programme.desc: A round-up of the day's news.

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: In Asia, the most densely populated continent, animals have developed extraordinary ways to seize the opportunities of the human world - from tigers entering a city to hunt easy prey to elephants stopping traffic to demand food from motorists. A small park in central Bangkok supports 300 giant lizards, whilst a flying squirrel in Taipei has made a cosy home in a school. Yet the changing human world creates unprecedented challenges – proboscis monkeys are forced to venture uncomfortably closer to humans, and swifts in Jerusalem face tough competition for nest sites.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May go to Vietnam and are told to travel the entire length of the country in just eight days, thereby achieving what the American military failed to do in ten years. First they must each buy suitable transport for the trip, but the several million dong they have in their pockets prove to be rather less money than they thought, especially in one of the most expensive car markets in the world. Nonetheless, the boys are resourceful and, with the wheels eventually sorted, they set off on one of the most spectacular and incredible road trips Top Gear has ever attempted.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: In a Top Gear special, Jeremy, Richard and James face one of their greatest challenges as all three are sent to Africa and each told to buy a second hand car costing no more than £1500. It must not be a 4x4 and must not be designed in any way to go off road. Which could be a problem, since their task is then to drive across the wilds of Botswana, negotiating massive salt pans, treacherous rivers and reserves full of animals, most of which will want to eat them. Along the way they face fierce heat, suffocating dust and an encounter with the Stig's African cousin in what becomes one of Top Gear's most epic adventures.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: In the first of a two-part Top Gear special, Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May are in Africa with a simple mission - to find the definitive source of the Nile. Over the years, many explorers claim to have already done just that, but the Top Gear trio believe that they can do better by travelling further and faster than any exploration team in history using only grit, ingenuity and three ageing estate cars.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: In the second part of the Top Gear special, Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May continue their epic African odyssey. Having survived insane traffic, lethal mudslides and some distinctly dubious map reading, the trio and their ailing estate cars reach the climax of their quest to find the definitive source of the Nile.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Two inept burglars stumble upon a moral dilemma during a break-in that could change their lives forever. Dark comedy drama about morality and consequences.

programme.desc: It’s knockout week, and there are just 14 amateur cooks left in the competition. The judges are increasing the pressure to see which contestants can hold their nerve.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Can artificial intelligence read emotions better than a human? Hannah explores the new technology that is creeping into our lives.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Vernon Kay is at the helm of this quiz all about the UK. The Traitors star Paul Gorton leads an unreliable tour of a different destination each day, with celebrity players battling it out to sort unbelievable facts from fiction. This week’s guests are EastEnders star Nitin Ganatra, the Reverend Kate Bottley and Gladiator Apollo, aka Alex Gray. The tour starts in Derry/Londonderry. A daily winner is declared at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the amount of beige on show in a Telford flat. Dion heads downwards to reveal an unexpected bonus in Leeds. In Suffolk, there are character features for Jacqui to uncover.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Exploring the capital city by tram, Michael Portillo travels to the extraordinary open-air museum of Memento Park in the suburbs. He discovers how a collection of imposing Soviet-era statues removed from the city following the fall of communism were placed here as a reminder of Hungary’s past. In the north east neighbourhood of Rákospalota, Michael visits Origo Studio, one of the largest in Europe. He learns how it’s attracting big name Hollywood filmmakers and gets the inside track on a series of thrilling stunts. Across the Danube in Óbuda, Michael tours the Roman city of Aquincum, a vital part of the empire’s defences and one of Hungary’s largest archaeological sites. He’s surprised to find its amphitheatre, once the scene of fierce gladiator battles, is larger than the Colosseum in Rome.

programme.title: Lucy Worsley Investigates
programme.desc: Lucy Worsley investigates one of history’s most dramatic break-ups: when, in 1776, America declared its independence from Great Britain, sparking the American Revolution. This eight-year war claimed thousands of lives and ended in a humiliating defeat for King George III. Lucy sets out to uncover why America chose this path and how Britain’s missteps fractured an empire and shook the monarchy, and asks whether this explosive split could have been avoided.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The unique quiz show where if a player gives an Impossible answer, they are immediately eliminated. Which of the 24 contestants will face the £10,000 question today?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Four more contenders face the black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. Clive Myrie hosts and asks the questions on their specialist subjects, which are Tudor rebellions, Christina Aguilera, the US space shuttle program and James Parkinson.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Under the Vines
programme.desc: Nic brings word of Oakley’s favourable write-up, news which has already reached an unimpressed Marissa. As Daisy and Louis help Tippy prepare for her speech, Griffin’s unexpected arrival blindsides everyone, especially Gus. Gala prep at Shimmering Lake takes an explosive turn, putting the Behind the Vines showcase dinner finale in jeopardy until Daisy offers an alternative that could save the day. Friends rally round, and Oakley is finally ready for the spotlight, but will it be a success? Vic and Nic have some exciting news, while Daisy and Louis share a special moment, interrupted by Simone, leaving Louis faced with an unenviable decision.

programme.title: The Secret Life of Elephants
programme.desc: Second in a series of three programmes revealing the emotional and dramatic lives of elephants in Kenya's Samburu reserve. Baby elephant Breeze is growing up fast, but with the dry season approaching, she is about to face her biggest test yet. Meanwhile, Breeze's teenage brother Buster seems intent on getting himself and Breeze into trouble. Outside the reserve, more trouble is brewing as people and elephants come into conflict. Elephant expert Iain Douglas-Hamilton sends daughter Saba on a mission to help one of their best-known elephants - Mountain Bull - who is on a collision course with farmers and villagers. Elsewhere, a marauding group of bulls cause havoc by breaking into fields and raiding crops. The team think they might have an unusual solution and will need the help of some African honey bees. Back in the reserve, a devastating drought takes hold and Breeze and her family are forced to compete with other elephants for food and water. Will baby Breeze survive these hard times?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel introduces a selection of fascinating finds from a recent visit to Harrogate, including a table fashioned from an ancient bedpost, the diary of a young lady who toured Great Britain in 1815, and a piece of naval scrimshaw.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Today Flog It! comes from Grimsby Minster in North East Lincolnshire. It's in the heart of a town which was a renowned fishing port. Antiques experts Christina Trevanion and Michael Baggott find great maritime memorabilia including a ships bell and a diver's knife. And Paul Martin meets a Grimsby trawler man on the very vessel he took to sea.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Cheryl Baker, Chris Bavin, Axel Blake and Sophie Willan take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Continuing his travels in Budapest, Michael Portillo begins in the small town of Huvösvölgy, in the hills above the city, at a surprising railway run almost entirely by children, dating back to the communist era. All of the staff, except for the train drivers, are volunteers aged ten to 14. Back in the city, he visits the former home of Béla Bartók, one of Hungary’s most famous pianists and composers, and learns how the country’s folk music inspired his work. Next, Michael heads across the Danube to the headquarters of the low-cost airline Wizz Air, one of the country’s post-communist success stories. At the pilot academy, he endures a stressful emergency landing and tries his hand at flying a plane.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Quiz show host and novelist Richard Osman takes on his other half, comedian, actress and Doctor Who star Ingrid Oliver, in a competition to find the most profitable antiques. Teaming up with experts Natasha Raskin Sharp and Raj Bisram, they head for the knick-knack shops of Norfolk with £400 each to spend. While Ingrid can’t resist a sad doggy face when it comes to works of art, she and Raj bravely come face to face with a dragon in Norwich. Richard and Natasha are rewarded with cake when they visit Norfolk’s last remaining watermill. Raj and Ingrid have high hopes for some expensive West German pottery, but the other team are discombobulated when their budget buy of a Scandinavian glass ashtray turns out to be a case of mistaken identity - will it go up in smoke at auction?

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: The pressure builds as chicks prepare to fledge and predators close in. The Springwatch team hope to capture even more intimate moments from the lives of the wildlife calling National Trust Crom home through their 24-hour remote camera surveillance. Away from Crom, Iolo Williams spends his final night live at Knepp, where rewilding is transforming the landscape. From free-roaming grazing animals to rare species returning against the odds, Iolo discovers how nature is reclaiming one of Britain’s most ambitious conservation projects.

programme.title: In Ten Pictures
programme.desc: How did Vladimir Putin emerge from a shadowy existence as a KGB agent in 1980s East Germany to become one of the most powerful men on the planet? This film examines Putin’s rise to power through his enduring relationship with images, and his innate understanding of their power.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Acting on a tip off, the Peelers storm a city centre flat on a drugs bust. Inside, a startled suspect is immediately cuffed and arrested while outside, the PSNI team search the nearby streets for the suspected big-time dealer they think may have fled the scene with more drugs. On Great Victoria Street in Belfast city centre, police attempt to arrest a man who refuses to comply with a search. The situation quickly escalates, and he is detained by a number of officers who use a spit guard and leg restraints. The man is taken into custody, where he continues to kick off. Officers and custody staff surround the man in his cell as they try to get him under control. Later, Stephen interviews the deputy chief constable, Bobby Singleton, and questions him about some PSNI tactics and officers’ use of force.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Katie Razzall.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: Surgeons drain all of their patient’s blood from his body to replace damaged arteries. A patient’s fertility is at risk without a complex operation to remove diseased bowel.

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: Knockout week continues, and the chefs must prove themselves enough to make it into their first professional kitchen.

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: It’s knockout week, and there are just 14 amateur cooks left in the competition. The judges are increasing the pressure to see which contestants can hold their nerve.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Continuing his travels in Budapest, Michael Portillo begins in the small town of Huvösvölgy, in the hills above the city, at a surprising railway run almost entirely by children, dating back to the communist era. At the pilot academy, he endures a stressful emergency landing and tries his hand at flying a plane.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Quiz show host and novelist Richard Osman takes on his other half, comedian, actress and Doctor Who star Ingrid Oliver, in a competition to find the most profitable antiques. Teaming up with experts Natasha Raskin Sharp and Raj Bisram, they head for the knick-knack shops of Norfolk with £400 each to spend. While Ingrid can’t resist a sad doggy face when it comes to works of art, she and Raj bravely come face to face with a dragon in Norwich. Richard and Natasha are rewarded with cake when they visit Norfolk’s last remaining watermill. Raj and Ingrid have high hopes for some expensive West German pottery, but the other team are discombobulated when their budget buy of a Scandinavian glass ashtray turns out to be a case of mistaken identity - will it go up in smoke at auction?

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: The pressure builds as chicks prepare to fledge and predators close in. Away from Crom, Iolo Williams spends his final night live at Knepp, where rewilding is transforming the landscape. programme.title: In Ten Pictures
programme.desc: How did Vladimir Putin emerge from a shadowy existence as a KGB agent in 1980s East Germany to become one of the most powerful men on the planet? This film examines Putin’s rise to power through his enduring relationship with images, and his innate understanding of their power.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Acting on a tip off, the Peelers storm a city centre flat on a drugs bust. Inside, a startled suspect is immediately cuffed and arrested while outside, the PSNI team search the nearby streets for the suspected big-time dealer they think may have fled the scene with more drugs. On Great Victoria Street in Belfast city centre, police attempt to arrest a man who refuses to comply with a search. The situation quickly escalates, and he is detained by a number of officers who use a spit guard and leg restraints. The man is taken into custody, where he continues to kick off. Officers and custody staff surround the man in his cell as they try to get him under control. Later, Stephen interviews the deputy chief constable, Bobby Singleton, and questions him about some PSNI tactics and officers’ use of force.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the amount of beige on show in a Telford flat. Dion heads downwards to reveal an unexpected bonus in Leeds. In Suffolk, there are character features for Jacqui to uncover.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Exploring the capital city by tram, Michael Portillo travels to the extraordinary open-air museum of Memento Park in the suburbs. He discovers how a collection of imposing Soviet-era statues removed from the city following the fall of communism were placed here as a reminder of Hungary’s past. In the north east neighbourhood of Rákospalota, Michael visits Origo Studio, one of the largest in Europe. He learns how it’s attracting big name Hollywood filmmakers and gets the inside track on a series of thrilling stunts. Across the Danube in Óbuda, Michael tours the Roman city of Aquincum, a vital part of the empire’s defences and one of Hungary’s largest archaeological sites. He’s surprised to find its amphitheatre, once the scene of fierce gladiator battles, is larger than the Colosseum in Rome.

programme.title: Lucy Worsley Investigates
programme.desc: Lucy Worsley investigates one of history’s most dramatic break-ups: when, in 1776, America declared its independence from Great Britain, sparking the American Revolution. This eight-year war claimed thousands of lives and ended in a humiliating defeat for King George III. Lucy sets out to uncover why America chose this path and how Britain’s missteps fractured an empire and shook the monarchy, and asks whether this explosive split could have been avoided.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul, Bob and trusty terrier Ted travel to Blakeney Point in North Norfolk for a sea-fishing adventure. Blakeney Point is a four-mile spit of shingle and sand beach bank, with the North Sea on one side and the Glaven Estuary on the other. It is a nature reserve and an important nesting ground for terns and gulls. There is also the chance they may spot a seal in the sea. After a day of mixed fortunes, they take a boat back to the car and head to their accommodation for the evening: Bear’s Cottage, which was built in 1856 and is surrounded by 200 acres of trees, including giant redwoods and noble firs.

programme.title: The Secret Life of Elephants
programme.desc: Second in a series of three programmes revealing the emotional and dramatic lives of elephants in Kenya's Samburu reserve. Baby elephant Breeze is growing up fast, but with the dry season approaching, she is about to face her biggest test yet. Meanwhile, Breeze's teenage brother Buster seems intent on getting himself and Breeze into trouble. Outside the reserve, more trouble is brewing as people and elephants come into conflict. Elephant expert Iain Douglas-Hamilton sends daughter Saba on a mission to help one of their best-known elephants - Mountain Bull - who is on a collision course with farmers and villagers. Elsewhere, a marauding group of bulls cause havoc by breaking into fields and raiding crops. The team think they might have an unusual solution and will need the help of some African honey bees. Back in the reserve, a devastating drought takes hold and Breeze and her family are forced to compete with other elephants for food and water. Will baby Breeze survive these hard times?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Continuing his travels in Budapest, Michael Portillo begins in the small town of Huvösvölgy, in the hills above the city, at a surprising railway run almost entirely by children, dating back to the communist era. All of the staff, except for the train drivers, are volunteers aged ten to 14. Back in the city, he visits the former home of Béla Bartók, one of Hungary’s most famous pianists and composers, and learns how the country’s folk music inspired his work. Next, Michael heads across the Danube to the headquarters of the low-cost airline Wizz Air, one of the country’s post-communist success stories. At the pilot academy, he endures a stressful emergency landing and tries his hand at flying a plane.

programme.title: Scrum V
programme.desc: Lauren Salter and guests preview Cardiff’s play-off match against the Stormers in the United Rugby Championship.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Lochs
programme.desc: Paul’s loch-hopping journey starts on the west coast on a wild and windswept stretch of Loch Hourn. Travelling inland, Paul reaches sheltered Loch Quoich, where he hears tales of Scotland’s last outlaw. On the shores of Loch Lochy, he meets a couple who had a memorable encounter with a monster from the deep called Lizzie. A detour south leads to a ruined bridge where the first shots were fired of the ’45. Paul then walks an old railway line above the Great Glen and inhales diesel smoke from a reeking shunter at a station undergoing restoration. A canal journey takes him to Fort Augustus, where he searches for the original fort. On Loch Ness, Paul meets a man who, when still a schoolboy, met the fastest man on water, John Cobb aka the Gentle Giant.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: The pressure builds as chicks prepare to fledge and predators close in. The Springwatch team hope to capture even more intimate moments from the lives of the wildlife calling National Trust Crom home through their 24-hour remote camera surveillance. Away from Crom, Iolo Williams spends his final night live at Knepp, where rewilding is transforming the landscape. From free-roaming grazing animals to rare species returning against the odds, Iolo discovers how nature is reclaiming one of Britain’s most ambitious conservation projects.

programme.title: In Ten Pictures
programme.desc: How did Vladimir Putin emerge from a shadowy existence as a KGB agent in 1980s East Germany to become one of the most powerful men on the planet? This film examines Putin’s rise to power through his enduring relationship with images, and his innate understanding of their power.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Acting on a tip off, the Peelers storm a city centre flat on a drugs bust. Inside, a startled suspect is immediately cuffed and arrested while outside, the PSNI team search the nearby streets for the suspected big-time dealer they think may have fled the scene with more drugs. On Great Victoria Street in Belfast city centre, police attempt to arrest a man who refuses to comply with a search. The situation quickly escalates, and he is detained by a number of officers who use a spit guard and leg restraints. The man is taken into custody, where he continues to kick off. Officers and custody staff surround the man in his cell as they try to get him under control. Later, Stephen interviews the deputy chief constable, Bobby Singleton, and questions him about some PSNI tactics and officers’ use of force.

programme.desc: Exploring the capital city by tram, Michael Portillo travels to the extraordinary open-air museum of Memento Park in the suburbs. He discovers how a collection of imposing Soviet-era statues removed from the city following the fall of communism were placed here as a reminder of Hungary’s past. In the north east neighbourhood of Rákospalota, Michael visits Origo Studio, one of the largest in Europe. He learns how it’s attracting big name Hollywood filmmakers and gets the inside track on a series of thrilling stunts. Across the Danube in Óbuda, Michael tours the Roman city of Aquincum, a vital part of the empire’s defences and one of Hungary’s largest archaeological sites. He’s surprised to find its amphitheatre, once the scene of fierce gladiator battles, is larger than the Colosseum in Rome.

programme.title: Lucy Worsley Investigates
programme.desc: Lucy Worsley investigates one of history’s most dramatic break-ups: when, in 1776, America declared its independence from Great Britain, sparking the American Revolution. This eight-year war claimed thousands of lives and ended in a humiliating defeat for King George III. Lucy sets out to uncover why America chose this path and how Britain’s missteps fractured an empire and shook the monarchy, and asks whether this explosive split could have been avoided.

Toodloo makes it over with ease, while Great BigHoo struggles, and Chickedy and Chick are just too small. Great BigHoo decides to help them by picking them up and throwing them. As Great BigHoo and Toodloo look on, Chickedy and Chick ride around the course and go over the jumps, until the Hooter calls the Twirlywoos home. They soon find a tiny one that has just poked its head above the soil - but where has it come from?

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Rebecca and Murphi are dealing with a glut of carrots from the vegetable patch, and they have made everything from carrot cake to carrot juice. This inspires Murphi’s first idea – a carton bunny rabbit. The Mini Monsters are making colourful caterpillars, and Rebecca’s uncle is snug as a bug in his woolly cardigan when he calls her on the Magic Monster Mirror. The Recycling Express brings an empty box, which Rebecca and Murphi transform into a cardboard kitty cat.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: A young Cornasaurolophus starts popping, which draws the attention of the Bananaraptors!

programme.title: Bluey

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Norrie is running late to Squirrel Club, so Duggee teaches the squirrels what a commute is – a journey that can take you from home to learn, work or play.

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk to a great place to play a train game. On the way, they find a ten-mile-long snake, make friends with a woodlouse, listen to the wind blowing through willow trees and even stomp like giants!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: We meet five-year-old Henry and his family: Mummy, Mama, and little sister Sophie. There’s lots of fun in store with a breakfast boogie and a visit to a farm. Back at home, they have some bouncy fun on the trampoline, and they find a tiny visitor in need of rescuing. But will they get the ladybird to safety?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Lola's making a traditional Spanish dish called empanadas for her friends. Lola begins by rolling out two pieces of pizza dough into big circles. She cooks one in the oven. Will Lola's friends find the empanadas tasty? Will they guess her special ingredient? There's a very exciting Spanish surprise waiting for her friends while they enjoy their meal!

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In today’s episode Maddie is listening for sounds. First, she discovers how wearing a hearing aid can help us hear more clearly. She meets 7 year old Zara who uses a hearing aid, before visiting the audiology department in a children’s hospital to see where hearing aids are made. Maddie finds out what happens when we have our hearing tested. She listens to different sounds through headphones so the Audiologist can see how well her ears hear sounds. Maddie then uses her special microscopic camera to see the tiny parts of the hearing aid before showing us what it’s like to have one fitted. Next, Maddie heads to a whistle factory to see how they are made. She uses her special camera to see big, strong stamping machines cut shapes out of brass and finds out how the cork ball gets put inside the whistle when it’s too big for the hole!

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Therapy dog Toffee and his owner, Helen, are on a mission to help their new neighbours, Kayla the vet and her daughter Tilly, on moving-in day.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet some colourful characters - the amazing mandrills, which are the largest species of monkey in the world. They get close enough to see the beautiful blue and red faces of the males. Next, Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet sand lizards. They are surrounded by many females, who blend in perfectly with their sandy home, as well as some colourful males, who are much easier to spot. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the wild connection is between these two incredible animals.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Evie pretends to be Waffle’s dog friend. She even wears a headband with doggy ears. Waffle loves it when they play together like this but Simon calls Evie for school - it is time to leave. Evie says her goodbyes together with Simon and Doug and she promises she will play with Waffle again later, when she returns home. Waffle is disappointed that his playmate has left but Jess cheers him up - she suggests they play doggy chase before she goes to work. Jess puts on doggy ears and chases Waffle on all fours into the bedroom where Jess’s mobile phone rings. It is Angela from the kennels, calling with news of a sad dog she wants Jess to examine. Jess assures Angela she will come right away and invites Waffle to join her. Waffle is very excited and when he arrives at the kennels with Jess, he still wants to play chase.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Baba is sick, so Oona tries to cheer him up with a special, shiny seashell.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Yukee is desperate to meet the worms that live in the soil beneath the garden. Learning that they only come out when it rains, Yukee tries to simulate the sound before realising that it’s the rhythm that the worms really love.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs are putting on a stage show for Mum - they've created characters, a story, costumes and songs. The only problem is, Dad keeps making noise with his DIY! Does he not realise they're trying to put on an epic show?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels meet a Scrufflelump in the woods, and despite Duggee’s reservations, take him in. But they soon learn the responsibilities of taking care of a pet.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: The Numberblocks make a new friend who likes to roll dice, and with Six in the mix, everything is a game. Learn all about the number 6 with Numberblock Six.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. It's race day - will V vroom vroom to victory?

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Ben meets Harry and Christopher for a camp-out in the forest. They pitch a tent and start a campfire. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble gets into a muddle trying to pitch a tent. There's hot chocolate and marshmallows in this spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words forest, tent and campfire.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: When the lights go out in the Home Dome, the Teletubbies get the giggles! The lights come back on again and there is Tubby Custard mess everywhere.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how chalk streams play an important role in their environment. They find out that they are a very special type of stream, with cool, clear water that is perfect for lots of plants to grow. They learn that many different creatures like to make their home in and around the streams too. On the way, they pretend to be kingfishers and herons, and take a close look at some animals that live in chalk streams.

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: It’s the Den’s summer fete, and Jaz is excited to do a chicken and egg mascot dance with her dad, but soon realises she’s double-booked herself and might not have time to do both.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: CBeebies’ very own motorbike rider Grace shows off three amazing machines that are all kinds of transport! Grace goes underground to drive a tube train, shows off a hanging railway and then drives a hydrogen boat.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: Miss Collie brings her pet stick insect, Woody, to class, but halfway through the day, Woody mysteriously vanishes! Dodge, Woofer, and Jazz spring into action, convinced a pup has taken him, and launch an investigation to track down the culprit. Just as Dodge thinks he’s cracked the case, they discover Woody was in his tank all along, showing off some surprising skills!

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Split is terrified of sliding down the necks of giant Broccolisaurus.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: Ranger Marsh recounts Shellington's journey to reunite a monitor lizard with his siblings.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: Peter Rabbit wants to grow up to be just like his late father - he has big paws to fill. But with his father's journal and the help of his best friends Benjamin and Lily, Peter is ready for some fun and delightful new discoveries. When Mr Tod tramples on the Shrew's precious dandelions, the angry Shrew vows revenge. But when Cotton-tail follows him into Mr Tod's lair, Peter, Lily and Benjamin must go on a dangerous mission to rescue them both!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: When the Squirrels search for Enid, they are surprised to hear her meow from the top of the Mighty Sugar Bun Mountain. The Squirrels prepare for the climb to rescue Enid, but first Duggee teaches them what they need to pack in their backpacks for a successful trip. The team walk through rocky terrain, grey skies, plentiful rain and snow blizzards but keep morale high as they learn how phrasing negative thoughts into helpful ones will let them overcome any challenges along the way. The Squirrels repeat their positive affirmations to keep climbing up the Sugar Bun as a team, and when they find themselves at the top of the mountain, they all give Enid a big hug. A successful rescue mission means Happy can have his nap on the sofa with Enid when they are back!

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: It's Sweetwood Spa Day, but Zigzag is so excited that she struggles to relax.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Prickly Pear arrives in the supermarket and tries to take over Evil Pea’s freezer. Supertato discovers that Prickly Pear isn’t mean at all and just needs some good friends.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings ban Weasy from playing on their toy train track after he destroys it and it has to be rebuilt. Annoyed, he decides to create his own mega course - no ducklings allowed!

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: An old map, mysterious clues and ancient secrets... Mojo and Bo are after the treasure of the Knights of Swoppiton! But Preston’s after it too, so they need to get there first.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: When Mum’s sister Brandy comes over for a visit, she brings Bluey and Bingo onesies.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: When Dad brings a pair of tenacious tickle crabs home from the beach, nowhere in the house is safe! His only hope of escaping their tickles is with the help of his true love.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Zog starts sleepwalking, wreaking havoc in the forest. Pearl and Gadabout need to work together to help him, but they can’t seem to put their personal disagreements aside.

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: Dr Ollie forgets who he asked to take the role of the wizard in his play! Ava’s memory-jogging machine helps him recall, but things get confusing at the nursery.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: It's early in the morning after the Brooklyn-Bells have returned from holiday and there's someone banging on their front door. It's Mrs Hobbs and she's furious. Waffle left Mrs Hobbs's kitchen taps running and now her home is flooded and there's water pouring out of her front door! But Jess and Simon will be Mrs Hobbs's 'knights in shining armour' - Sir Jess and Sir Simon Brooklyn-Bells to the rescue!

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi, Dash and Jake set off on a camping adventure, determined to stick to their wizarding scout plan - no wishes allowed! When they realise the original plan won’t work, Rafi suggests making a new one instead. With teamwork, flexibility and the right wish, the Wizard Wagon takes flight and carries them to the perfect camping spot at sunset. Rafi learns that plans can change, and sometimes the best adventures come from making a new one together.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran visit the park cafe, where JoJo tries the daily special on the menu for the first time. When they get home, they decide to make a play cafe in Gran Gran's garden for JoJo's toys to visit. JoJo makes a menu and Gran Gran helps her make the play food. JoJo learns how much fun it is to run a cafe – especially when you have a special on the menu.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Sarah and Duck learn to bobsleigh and have a speedy, snowy adventure with Scarf Lady's help.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Major invents a giant magnet. Everything metal flies towards it, from soup tankards to knitting needles. Mother and Granny tell Major to take it outside where it can't do any harm. But then the Iron Chicken lands, and after an unfortunate incident where she gets stuck to the magnet, she tells Major, Tiny and Small about a strange sound she has heard in space. They investigate and find a moon whale trapped in an old metal rocket booster. The magnet turns out to be the perfect thing for the rescue.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa are playing a copying game. BaBa likes copying MeMo, but at the Play Tree, MeMo wants to play a different game with some beepy horns. BaBa still wants to copy MeMo and is sad at Yummy Time when MeMo and the Yummies play something else. MeMo doesn’t want BaBa to be sad. With the help of the Yummies, MeMo finds a happy way to compromise.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: Makka Pakka has a pile of six stones. He gives one stone to Igglepiggle and one stone to Upsy Daisy. Upsy Daisy tucks her stone safely in her bed. Makka Pakka gives a stone to each of the Tombliboos. The teeny tiny Pontipines take Makka Pakka's last stone.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Gregory Porter sings the classic What a Wonderful World as a special Bedtime Story.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s the exceptional painter Spinach creating Kiwi’s portrait, if Kiwi can keep still.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Sula, Pando, Flop and Padget all have a knack, a special thing that only they can do. Bing is frustrated when all his own knacks are easy for everyone else to do too. When Pando accidentally hurts Bing's ear, they are all in for a surprise, as Bing discovers he does have a knack that no-one else can do.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Laa-Laa leaves muddy footprints on a rug but magically makes them disappear by singing. Meanwhile, the children in Tummy Tales enjoy a squelchy walk through mud with bare feet.

programme.title: Tee and Mo
programme.desc: Preschool animation about a baby monkey and his mother. Tee and Mo are on a car trip to the beach, but Tee runs out of entertainment immediately. It's going to be a long trip...

With herself and the Corn Cobs stacked on top of each other, they initially get the veggies to run away. Supertato wonders if the monster is just looking for a new friend, so he chases after it! When one of the arms falls off the monster, the Tato Team realise it’s just someone in a costume. They find out it was Evil Pea all along!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing is teaching Charlie how to throw, but when he throws the ball in the lounge it knocks the fruit over! Bing starts to explain, but Charlie interrupts, leaving Flop to believe Charlie did it. Bing happily shows Charlie how to voosh Squeaky instead, but it flies out of his hands and hits Flop's tray of snacks! After some encouragement, Bing tells Flop the truth and apologises.

programme.desc: Betty’s new ice cream flavour is so light, it makes everybody in town float in the air. How will Mojo and Bo get everyone’s feet back on the ground? By floating up there with them!
